title: Properness cancellation for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X,Y,Z$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is separated if its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], tested on scheme base changes. It is quasi-compact if for every affine scheme $W$ mapping to its target the algebraic space pullback to $W$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. It is of finite type if it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Point spaces carry the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. It is universally closed if every algebraic-space base change is a closed map of point spaces. Proper means separated, of finite type, and universally closed, agreeing with [def-weil-proper-morphism] for schemes. Let $u:X\to Y$ and $v:Y\to Z$ be morphisms. If $v\circ u$ is proper and $v$ is separated, then $u$ is proper. No scheme representability, Noetherian, finite-presentation or local quasi-finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put $h=v\circ u$ and $P=X\times_ZY$, with projections $p_X,p_Y$. The sheaf fibre-product universal property gives $\gamma=(\mathrm{id}_X,u):X\to P$ and $a=(u\circ p_X,p_Y):P\to Y\times_ZY$. The square with top $u:X\to Y$, bottom $a$, left $\gamma$ and right $\Delta_v:Y\to Y\times_ZY$ is cartesian: on every scheme test, its pullback sections are triples $(x,y,y_0)$ with $u(x)=y_0=y$, hence uniquely sections $x$ of $X$. This identification is natural in the test scheme. Also $p_Y\circ\gamma=u$.

source.place: Tag 04NX (lemma-universally-closed-permanence), graph factorization; Tag 03KO (lemma-semi-diagonal), via lemma-fibre-product-after-map.

proof.text: Since $v$ is separated, $\Delta_v$ is a representable closed immersion by the stated definition. Its pullback $\gamma$ is a representable closed immersion: for any scheme $T\to P$, the test $T\times_PX\to T$ identifies by the cartesian square with $T\times_{Y\times_ZY}Y\to T$, which is a closed immersion of schemes by the definition of $\Delta_v$. Thus no scheme representability of $u$ or $v$ is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 03KO (lemma-semi-diagonal), part (3); representable closed immersions are tested after scheme base change.

proof.text: Apply the closed-immersion properness lemma to $\gamma:X\to P$ to obtain that $\gamma$ is proper; in particular $\gamma$ is separated, locally of finite type on etale scheme charts and universally closed. Since $h:X\to Z$ is proper by hypothesis, its base change along $v:Y\to Z$ is proper. This base change is exactly $p_Y:P=X\times_ZY\to Y$; so $p_Y$ is separated, quasi-compact in the affine-test sense of the statement, locally of finite type on etale scheme charts and universally closed. Both factors of $u=p_Y\circ\gamma$ thus have these properties.

source.place: Tag 04NX, graph factorization, using Tag 04XZ (lemma-closed-immersion-proper) and Tag 04WP (lemma-base-change-proper).

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of $u$, in the sense of the statement. Let $W$ be an affine scheme and $W\to Y$ a morphism. Put $X_W=X\times_YW$ and $P_W=P\times_YW$. By transitivity of sheaf fibre products, $P_W\cong X\times_ZW$ (with $W\to Z$ the composite $v$-map) and, since $u=p_Y\circ\gamma$, $X_W\cong X\times_PP_W$. Since $h$ is quasi-compact, there is a surjective etale map $h_U\to P_W$ with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme. Its base change $U'=h_U\times_{P_W}X_W\to X_W$ is again surjective etale by the covering clause of the fibre-product lemma. Also $U'\cong h_U\times_PX$ is the scheme test of $\gamma$ along $U\to P_W\to P$, so by step 2 it is a closed subscheme of $U$; its underlying space is a closed subset of the quasi-compact space $U$, hence $U'$ is a quasi-compact scheme. So $X_W$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, and $u$ is quasi-compact. Unlike the composition lemma for proper maps, whose quasi-compactness is the topological one (inverse images of quasi-compact opens; weaker for non-quasi-separated targets, e.g. $\mathbf A^1\to\mathbf A^1/\mathbf Z$), this is the affine-test notion of the statement.

source.place: Tag 03HG (lemma-composition-quasi-compact), proof omitted ('transitivity of fibre products'), written out for $u=p_Y\circ\gamma$ with Tag 04CG (closed immersions are quasi-compact).

proof.text: Local finite type and separatedness of $u$. Algebraic spaces are Deligne--Mumford stacks with the stack notions agreeing with the space notions, and local finite type on etale scheme charts is stable under composition; since $\gamma$ and $p_Y$ are locally of finite type (step 3), so is $u=p_Y\circ\gamma$. Since $\gamma$ and $p_Y$ are separated (their diagonals are representable closed immersions, step 3), the composite $u$ is separated by the composition clause for separated morphisms of algebraic spaces. Together with step 4, $u$ is of finite type.

source.place: Tag 03XG (lemma-composition-finite-type) and Tag 03KQ (lemma-composition-separated), applied to the factorization of Tag 04NX.

proof.text: Universal closedness of $u$. Let $Y'\to Y$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces, $X'=X\times_YY'$ and $P'=P\times_YY'$. By transitivity of sheaf fibre products $X'\cong X\times_PP'$, and $X'\to Y'$ is the composite $X'\to P'\to Y'$ of the base change of $\gamma$ along $P'\to P$ and the base change of $p_Y$ along $Y'\to Y$. Both induce closed maps of point spaces by step 3. The point map of a composite is the composite of the point maps, since both send the class of a field-valued representative $x$ to the class of its image; a composite of closed maps is closed. Hence $u$ is universally closed. With steps 4 and 5, $u$ is separated, of finite type and universally closed, that is, proper. All objects and tests stay over the given $S$.

source.place: Tag 03IU (lemma-composition-universally-closed), applied to the factorization of Tag 04NX.

That is strictly weaker than the item's affine-test notion: A^1->A^1/Z has |f| qc, but A^1 x_Y A^1 is a disjoint union of copies of A^1 indexed by Z, so f is not qc. Step 6 gets universal closedness elementarily from transitivity of fibre products and composition of point maps (def-a1-space-point-topology). The proper-composition citation is dropped.
